title: TS-40d Delete python/ and replace the Python-dependent tooling
description: Part of the flip (chatticus-6f27c5). Delete python/ entirely (including wiki_publish and channel_migration), python/behave.ini, the CI python job and the pins. First replace every non-Python consumer of Python found by the re-audit: semantic-release reads python/pyproject.toml; CDK bundles Python Lambdas from python/; conversation/test/ported-features-manifest.test.ts reads python/behave.ini (rewrite so cucumber-js is the only runner); the template drift check and the customer-provisioning test read python/src/chatticus/assets (move the assets); the conversation CI job installs Python only for moto (use a pinned moto container or a Node alternative, no python tree); infra deploy scripts call python3 for JSON (use node or jq). Port conversation/bin/chat.ts (demo_cli, currently a stub) if still wanted. Delete obsolete Gherkin and record each removed scenario in the closing comment: messages.feature user-active-turns and its six undefined turn scenarios, demo_cli list-in-flight, @wip delegated_authority and escalation_approval, the seven private-repo waitlist/survey/contact features.

comments.author: home
comments.text: PR A merged (466): npm semantic-release replaces python-semantic-release (numbering continues from the latest tag v0.43.0 on main; breaking changes map to minor, plus the guard-pre-1-0 job), cucumber list renamed features/cucumber-features.txt with no behave.ini dependency (751 scenarios identical before and after), template drift check and provisioning test read infra/assets, CI moto is a pinned service container (npm run moto:start locally), budgets script uses awk. The first real run of the new release path happens at the first release after the develop to main promotion (untestable before). Next: PR B deletes python/, the Python step files, the obsolete features recorded in docs/PYTHON_RETIREMENT_SCENARIOS.md, the CI python job, budget-rollup-contract.test.ts.

right_now_summary: PR B is removing the Python tree, CI job, and obsolete scenarios after the tooling migration.
